# leticode.toml

<!-- generated by `letibot --config-reference --markdown leticode.toml`; do not edit -->

Location: user: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/letibot/leticode.toml (else ~/.config/letibot); project: the nearest leticode.toml at or above the workspace

which models answer, and the session, queue, head and sandbox settings, at two levels

A change takes effect: a session reads it when it opens, so the next session has it; the daemon reads [gc], [docker], [firecode] and [memory] at start, so a change there needs a daemon restart

## `top level`

Order: command line, project file, user file, providers.toml. A key a level does not set falls through.

| key | type | default | level | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main_model` | string | --provider, else providers.toml [default], else local | both, project wins | model the session's turns go to |
| `subagent_model` | string | the parent's model | both, project wins | default model for `task` spawns |
| `gatekeeper_model` | string | providers.toml [gatekeeper] model, else the session's | both, project wins | guard model |
| `judge_model` | string | as gatekeeper_model | both, project wins | same seat as gatekeeper_model; two different values are refused |
| `fallback` | list of models \| [fallback] table | providers.toml [fallback] models | the level that sets it replaces the other | models to move to when the session's model is out, in order |
| `fallback_after_timeouts` | int >= 1 | 3 | both, project wins | consecutive model timeouts before a fallback move |

## `[fallback]`

Table form of `fallback`: the list for one limited model. Lookup: exact model, then `provider/*`, then `*`.

| key | type | default | level | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<model>` | non-empty list | none | as fallback | list for that model; key is `provider/model`, `provider/*` or `*` |

## `[provider]`

Usage limits and model API deadlines. A plugin layer answering `limit_decide` decides a limit in place of `on_limit`, `wait_if_within` and the fallback lists.

| key | type | default | level | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `on_limit` | "wait" \| "switch" | switch with a fallback, else wait | both, project wins | on a usage limit: park until the reset, or move to the next fallback |
| `wait_if_within` | span (45m, 1h30m, 90s, 2d, 0) | 45m | both, project wins | with switch: a reset this close is waited for anyway; 0 never waits |
| `limit_probe` | list of spans | [2m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h] | both, project wins | a park re-tries the refused request on these steps before its reset, the last repeating; [] never |
| `fallback` | list of models | none | as fallback | the top-level fallback list; both set to different lists is refused |
| `slow_notice_seconds` | int >= 1 | 15 | both, project wins | silence before the "model slow" notice |
| `first_byte_seconds` | int >= 1 | 60 | both, project wins | silence before the first byte that fails the round |
| `answer_seconds` | int >= 1 | 600 | both, project wins | budget for the whole answer |

| `weekly` | list of int 1..100 | [70, 95] | both, project wins | thresholds for a 7-day window |
| `monthly` | list of int 1..100 | [70, 95] | both, project wins | thresholds for a month window |

## `[exec]`

| key | type | default | level | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto_background` | bool | true | both, project wins | move a call to the background past the threshold |
| `foreground_seconds` | int >= 1 | 60 | both, project wins | foreground threshold |
| `job_dead_after_seconds` | int | 1800 | both, project wins | a job with no output and no CPU this long is dead; 0 = check off |
| `io_wbps` | size | none | both, project wins | io.max write bytes/s on every job (`200M`); needs io delegated |
| `io_wiops` | int | none | both, project wins | io.max write ops/s on every job; needs io delegated |
| `disk_floor` | percent or size | 5% | both, project wins | free space on a job's filesystems below which the top writers in the last 60s are stopped; 0 = off |
| `disk_floor_action` | freeze \| kill | freeze | both, project wins | what the floor does to them; `job_resume` thaws a frozen job |
| `io_pressure_full` | percent | 60 | both, project wins | system io `full` pressure (avg10) that, held for 20s, throttles the top writer through io.max; 0 = off |
| `disk_watch` | list of paths | ["/build", $CARGO_TARGET_DIR] | both, project wins | filesystems the floor watches besides each job's cwd; replaces the default |
| `tasks_max` | int | 512 | both, project wins | processes one job's cgroup may hold (`pids.max`); a job that forks past it is ended; 0 = no cap |

## `[tools]`

A round's adjacent read-class calls (`read`, `grep`, `glob` and the rest whose schema declares read access) run at once, up to the pool's width; every other call - a write, an edit, a command, a job, a session verb, an unknown name - waits for all of them and they wait for it, so the order of effects is the order the model proposed. Results and their rows stay in that order either way.

| key | type | default | level | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `parallel` | bool | true | both, project wins | run a round's adjacent reads at once; false runs every call of the round one at a time |

## `[output]`

Over either cap a tool result keeps its head and tail inline and one seam line naming the read_spill locator for the middle. The middle is kept on disk per project and survives a restart. A tool's own tighter cap still applies; --spill-inline wins over inline_bytes, --spill-dir moves the store, `letibot holds` lists it there, and an older daemon's per-session spills under it are still read.

| key | type | default | level | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inline_bytes` | int | 51200 | both, project wins | most bytes a result keeps inline; 0 = no byte cap |
| `inline_lines` | int | 2000 | both, project wins | most lines a result keeps inline; 0 = no line cap |
| `spill_budget` | size | 2G | both, project wins | most bytes one project's spill store keeps under <data dir>/spills/<project>; over it the least recently read spill is evicted and read_spill says when; 0 = keep all |

## `[mcp.<name>]`

One MCP server per NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`, no `__`), stdio by `command` or streamable HTTP by `url` (http:// or https://; no OAuth, a token goes in `headers`). Its tools are reached through `mcp_search` and `mcp_call` as `NAME__tool`; the two doors seat only when a server is configured. Every call is a network call under the gate; preapprove with permission.json `{"mcp_call": {"NAME__*": "allow"}}`. Results fall under [output]. One process per distinct server, shared by the sessions naming it; a server that fails to start is reported once and the rest start. One that dies later is restarted on the next call, retried at 0.5 s doubling to 30 s. `/mcp` lists the servers with state, tools and pid or url; `/mcp reload` re-reads [mcp] and the pinned `.mcp.json` and starts added, stops removed and restarts changed servers (command, args, env, url, headers), leaving the rest running, and a call in flight finishes on the old process; `/mcp restart NAME` restarts one. At turn start a changed file (mtime, then sha256) or a stdio binary with a new mtime runs the same reload once, said in one `mcp:` row. No daemon restart is needed. A `notifications/tools/list_changed` lists its tools again. A project leticode.toml's [mcp] is reported and never started; a checkout's `.mcp.json` starts only under [mcp_projects].

| key | type | default | level | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string | none | user only | program to run as a stdio server; set this or url |
| `args` | list of strings | [] | user only | its arguments |
| `env` | table of strings | {} | user only | variables added to its environment |
| `url` | string | none | user only | http:// or https:// endpoint of a streamable HTTP server; set this or command |
| `headers` | table of strings | {} | user only | headers sent with every HTTP request |
| `timeout_seconds` | int >= 1 | 60 | user only | deadline for start, listing and each call |
| `enabled` | bool | true | user only | false keeps the table and starts nothing |

## `[mcp_projects]`

A checkout's `.mcp.json` (`{"mcpServers": {NAME: {command, args, env} or {type: "http", url, headers}}}`, the file pi, Claude Code and Cursor read) starts its servers only when `pinned` holds that file's exact path at the sha256 of its bytes, because a cloned repository or an edit inside a trusted tree would otherwise start processes. Its stdio servers run in the workspace with a cleared environment. A name the user's [mcp] also has is the user's. Unpinned or changed, the file's servers are named in one `mcp_server` warning per open, with the line that pins the bytes on disk, and not started.

| key | type | default | level | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pinned` | table of path to sha256 | {} | user only | absolute .mcp.json paths (`~/` allowed) and the sha256 their servers start at |
| `trusted` | list of paths | [] | user only | absolute directories; starts nothing alone, the warning names the pin for a checkout under one |

## `[peering]`

Two boxes' room coordinators link over one LAN on a shared cookie file (`~/.config/letibot/cookie`, mode 0600). No cookie file means no peering at all. The box's keys are the user file's; `introduce` is the project's.

| key | type | default | level | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool | true | user only | false keeps a box that has a cookie from peering at all |
| `port` | int 1..65535 | the kernel's choice | user only | TCP port links between coordinators arrive at |
| `group` | IPv4 address | 239.255.41.7 | user only | multicast group the beacons go to |
| `group_port` | int 1..65535 | 47311 | user only | UDP port the beacons go to, shared by every box on the LAN |
| `introduce` | bool | true | project only | false keeps this project's seats from being introduced to the same repository on another box |

## `[queue]`

The merge queue reads the project file only, except the three census keys.

| key | type | default | level | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stuck_after_seconds` | int >= 1 | 900 | both, project wins | a row stuck this long goes into the census |
| `stuck_repeat_seconds` | int >= 1 | 7200 | both, project wins | how often the census repeats |
| `mute` | list of repositories | [] | both, joined | repositories the session is not woken for |
| `target` | string | main, else master, else checked out | project only | branch this project lands on |
| `merge_via_session` | bool | false | project only | a review that cannot run goes to the main session |
| `red_target` | "fix" \| "raise" | fix | project only | what a red target triggers |
| `gate_carry` | list of paths | [] | project only | gitignored inputs copied into the landing tree |
| `reviewers` | "host" \| "vm" | host | project only | where reviewers run |
| `gate_host` | hosts.toml name | this machine | project only | machine the gate runs on |
| `gate_poll_seconds` | seconds, 0.1 to 9 | 5.0 | project only | wait between two polls of a running step; each poll is also the step's heartbeat |
| `gate_in` | "host" \| "firecode" | host | project only | gate steps run in a firecode VM |
| `reviewer_skills` | list of skills | [] | project only | skills preloaded into reviewers |
| `gate_train` | int >= 1 | 1 | project only | approved branches gated as one stack; a red stack is bisected |
| `reviewers_at_once` | int >= 1 | placement's | project only | concurrent reviewers |
| `reviewer_hosts` | list; ["*"] = all | ["local"] | project only | hosts a host reviewer may use |
| `reviewers_run_suites` | bool | false | project only | reviewers may run whole test suites, not only named tests |
| `grant_ttl_hours` | int >= 1 | 24 | project only | how long a session answer on a relayed reviewer card covers the queue |
| `gate_deadline_minutes` | int >= 1 | 30 | project only | one gate run's deadline, counted from when the box's gate lock is held |

## `[subagents]`

A spawn over a cap waits for a running child to answer, or is refused. A spawn with the objective of a running child is refused, naming it. Review-queue reviewers are outside these caps.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_running` | int >= 1 | 8 | both, project wins | children one root session's tree runs at once |
| `daemon_max_running` | int >= 1 | 32 | user only | children the whole daemon runs at once |
| `when_full` | "queue" \| "refuse" | "queue" | both, project wins | a spawn over a cap waits for a place, or fails naming the running children |
